questions.text: What is the primary function of the Trinidad and Tobago Central Depository (TTCD) when an investor buys shares through a licensed broker?
options: It guarantees the execution speed of all limit orders placed on the exchange.
It holds share certificates electronically in a digital vault, eliminating paper certificates.
It determines daily stock price ceilings and floors based on corporate profit releases.
It acts as the primary regulatory body licensing stockbrokers across the local market.
questions.explanation: The TTCD serves as a secure digital vault that stores share certificates electronically, doing away with physical paper certificates.

questions.text: How does a limit order differ from a market order when buying or selling shares on an exchange?
options: A limit order guarantees immediate trade execution regardless of the prevailing price.
A limit order gives total price control by executing only at a specified price or better, whereas a market order prioritizes immediate execution.
A limit order automatically routes shares through the securities commission instead of a broker.
A limit order tracks the overall composite index to adjust trade pricing automatically.
questions.explanation: A limit order ensures a trade occurs only at the designated price floor/ceiling or better, sacrificing guaranteed immediate execution for complete price control.

questions.text: True or false: Purchasing stock in a publicly listed company makes an investor a partial owner of that actual corporate enterprise.
questions.explanation: Buying shares in a listed company grants the investor partial ownership of the real corporate business.

questions.text: True or false: The TTSE Composite Index requires investors to manually check every individual stock to measure overall market direction.
questions.explanation: The TTSE Composite Index tracks the combined performance of listed companies to provide a quick snapshot of overall market trends without needing to check each stock individually.
